items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: And I had this man, you know, Marlon, Lawrence Vega, running the band.

ctx.x: I was up there. But I had to get back on account of so much contracts coming in, you understand. I had to depend on her. You see? And I had this man, you know, Marlon, Lawrence Vega, running the band. He always has. Cornet players. Oh, a mockable cornet players. So was Richie Brunitz. Oh, very good.
How was Nick LaRocca in those days? Oh, brother.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: Well, Lawrence Vega played with you. Yeah. And Pacquet and Dave Perkins and you, I forgot who the others were

ctx.x: Then I had another, just that quick, really. I see above the staff, Richie Brunus. Little Vega was the finest trumpet player that was in this man's town. Lawrence Vega. That kid could play a horn. Ragtime? Yeah. Yeah, Lawrence Vega. Brother, that boy, oh, he was young.

He played, that time he played with him and Pacquet and Dave Perkins. Huh. Well, Lawrence Vega played with you. Yeah. And Pacquet and Dave Perkins and you, I forgot who the others were, but anyhow, that's really, and you know Pacquet played good music. Pacquet played good music.
You heard of Ashil Pacquet playing clarinet, haven't you? He played good, he played good.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: We had one man by the very, uh, Lawrence Vega and this part of Parquet.

ctx.x: What kind of music? What kind of songs did you play?

What kind of songs? Mm-hmm. Well, all of our own composition. Your own composition? Yes. We had one man by the very, uh, Lawrence Vega and this part of Parquet. Well, in fact, the rest of them boys, they'd be with them all kinds of funny stuff. The first thing you know, when they'd get into the house with me and a bunch of kids, they'd want to try to see if they could play that stuff over again. Mm-hmm. And sure enough, they used us. Now, there was this Liberty Stable Blues, they call it. Liberty Stable Blues?…
